newsitem.title: TANZANIA: More refugees flee Zaire for Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: More refugees flee Zaire for Tanzania.

text.p: Some 5,000 war refugees have arrived in Tanzania from eastern Zaire over the past week, the U.N. refugee agency said on Thursday.
Lennart Kotsalainen, head of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Tanzania, told Reuters the refugees came from the small Zairean town of Fizi on the shores of Lake Tanganyika.
He blamed the latest influx on fighting between Zairean rebels and the army.

Zairean rebels of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) have been fighting to overthrow President Mobutu Sese Seko since October. They now control a large part of eastern Zaire.
Citing latest UNHCR figures, Kotsalainen said about 37,000 Zaireans had fled across the lake since November.
In addition to the refugee crisis caused by war in eastern Zaire, UNHCR was assisting an estimated 500 refugees crossing daily into Tanzania to escape ethnic violence in neighbouring Burundi.

Last month, the Tanzanian government ordered more than 500,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees living in camps in northwest Ngara region to return home by the end of 1996. Kotsalainen said UNHCR estimated 480,000 had since returned.
